readings.D0: one task process and one loaded instance per model in every RocketRide cell (docs: one SentenceTransformer; video: one RF-DETR LWDETR and one SentenceTransformer); LlamaIndex one worker process
readings.D1: the stage stamps and the timed service move nothing readable and change no chunk
readings.H1: the one task process runs no more documents at once than asyncio's default executor has threads (see H1); more in flight only queue at admission
readings.H2: the interpreter lock is not the ceiling; the 'about half the cores' reading is the drain tail (post-hoc: most vCPUs have a runnable thread while every document is in flight)
readings.H7: the debugger is attached in production, but its cost is below the RocketRide docs floor
readings.H5: no Tika feature explains the tail; isolated Tika parses the eleven in seconds
readings.E1: the tail lives in the engine's own parse path: inline-image extraction with a process spawned per embedded image
readings.H6: no parser clears the pre-registered rule on the full corpus: warm isolated Tika parses the 11 about as fast as pypdfium2 (the smoke's cold-JVM Tika time did not reproduce) and every alternative returns empty on documents Tika extracts; the tail is the engine's wrapper (E1), not the parser
readings.V1: at matched T=4 one LlamaIndex instance is materially faster than one RocketRide instance, in-session on both pairs
readings.V2: both arms hold their device lock nearly the whole window and the forward pass is nearly all of the hold; RocketRide's forward pass is slower at the same T although both images carry identical libraries and build the model identically, so the gap is in how the forward pass runs inside RocketRide's process, not in the work around it (post-hoc: about the same CPU per frame on fewer busy cores; cause untraced)
readings.V3: RocketRide holds its device lock around the whole facade call per frame; LlamaIndex holds its lock around a video's whole frame loop
